lines.text: One field line, anchored in the northern and southern hemispheres.
A charged particle circles its field line. Circling alone never carries it to another.
Toward the feet the field crowds together, and the particle is turned around.
It bounces, for as long as nothing scatters it.
Same particles, seen from above the north pole.
They drift right round the planet — and they go opposite ways.
Ions drift west. Electrons drift east.
They do not cancel. They add.
One westward current, tens of thousands of kilometres across.
So the field measured at the ground goes down.
That dip is Dst. It is how the size of a magnetic storm is stated.
